text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on May 11 in history:
330 - Constantinople was dedicated as the new capital of the Roman Empire. It was named after the Emperor Constantine and built over the ancient city of Byzantium.
1686 - Otto von Guericke, German physicist who demonstrated the vacuum, died. Also invented the first air pump.
1745 - The Battle of Fontenoy took place in Belgium, where French forces defeated the British and their allies during the War of the Austrian Succession.
1778 - William Pitt the Elder, British statesman, died. He conducted most of the Seven Years' War (1756-73) which secured Britain a huge new empire.
1812 - British Prime Minister Spencer Perceval was assassinated by a bankrupt broker, John Bellingham, as he entered the House of Commons.
1858 - Minnesota became the 32nd state of the Union.
1867 - The independence and neutrality of the duchy of Luxembourg was guaranteed by the European powers under the Treaty of London.
1871 - British astronomer Sir John Herschel died. He added over 500 nebulae and clusters of stars to those already known.
1888 - Irving Berlin, U.S. composer, born. He composed music for several musicals, including "Annie Get Your Gun", and also wrote "Alexander's Ragtime Band".
1904 - Salvador Dali, Spanish surrealist painter, born.
1931 - The failure of Credit-Anstalt, Austria's largest bank, marked the beginning of the financial collapse of Central Europe.
1943 - U.S. amphibious forces landed on Attu in the Aleutians, the first American territory to be recaptured by the U.S. from the Japanese.
1949 - Siam changed its name to Thailand.
1949 - Israel was admitted to the United Nations.
1960 - The world's longest liner, SS France, was launched.
1967 - Britain, Denmark and Ireland formally applied to join the European Economic Community.
1981 - Bob Marley, Jamaican-born singer who with his group The Wailers popularized reggae, died of cancer.
1985 - 56 people died and more than 200 were injured when fire engulfed the main stand at Bradford City football ground in northern England.
1987 - The Indian government imposed direct rule on Punjab because of the terror campaign being waged by Sikh extremists.

1988 - (Harold Adrian Russell) 'Kim' Philby, British intelligence officer and journalist, died. He was the 'third man' who enabled fellow spies Guy Burgess and Donald Maclean to escape to Russia in 1951.
1991 - Ho Dam, senior member of North Korea's communist party and former foreign minister, died. As foreign minister in 1977, he was the first senior North Korean official to visit the U.S.
1992 - EC foreign ministers decided to recall their ambassadors from Belgrade and to seek Yugoslavia's suspension from the CSCE.
1994 - Deir Al-Balah became the first Gaza town to come under Palestinian self-rule.
1994 - Haiti's military-backed government installed Emile Jonassaint as new provisional president.
1994 - Media tycoon Silvio Berlusconi was installed as Italy's prime minister at the head of a coalition government that brought neo-fascists to power for the first time since World War Two.
1994 - President Nelson Mandela named his main black political rival, Zulu chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi, and his estranged wife Winnie, as members of South Africa's new government of national unity.
1996 - A ValuJet Airlines DC-9 jet with 110 people on board crashed in the swampy Everglades near Miami International Airport. There were no survivors.
